interface.shortDescription: SSH to your servers from chat
interface.longDescription:
SSH access to your servers from ChatGPT: run commands, read and write files over SFTP, query databases and watch server health — on the Linux servers, VPS and cloud machines you connected. You never paste an SSH private key or password into ChatGPT.

Ask ChatGPT to check disk space and memory, tail a log, restart a service, edit a config, install a package, run a migration in the background, or run one command on several servers at once. It can list tables and run queries on Postgres, MySQL and other databases through the same path, and it can read the metrics and alerts Termalin's monitoring collects — CPU, memory, disk, load, failed services, certificates — so "how are my servers doing?" is answered from data.

How access works: your servers connect outward through Termalin Connectors (a one-line install, no open inbound port). Each command is authenticated with a short-lived certificate, and ChatGPT gets access through OAuth from your termal.in account, after you approve it on a consent screen. Your SSH keys, passwords and tokens stay on your side; the chat only receives command output.

You stay in control: per-connection policy (full access, an allowlist of commands, or read-only), a note on each server telling the AI what to be careful with, a full audit trail of every command, and one-click disconnect from your account page. Works alongside the Termalin desktop app (Windows, macOS, Linux), the iOS app and the web cabinet, but needs none of them to be open.

To get started, sign in at termal.in and install a Connector on a server (one command): https://termal.in/account
